coverage: Researched on 2026-10-31 by four parallel searches, one per group of domains, each told to report only what a fetched page carried and to list pages that would not load. Quotes were captured through a fetch tool that summarises pages; a sample of five (Viasat contract, Resende 70 percent, Santos Dumont integrator and operator, P-78 integration, Mero 3 subsea scope) was re-fetched and matched verbatim, and the rest still need a verbatim audit. Official sources that would not load are listed as blocked in each record: butantan.gov.br (403), planalto.gov.br decrees (blocked), gov.br/mcti (bot check), the LNCC expansion page (401), ceitec-sa.com (503), the Navy CTMSP page (403), Embraer's E2 page (404). Where a TCU ruling or a Diário Oficial page was read, it was read from a copy hosted by Poder360 that carries the official authenticity code. Searched and not recorded: Bipe, the messaging project SOV-2 names. No fetched page mentions it, so it has no record and nothing here says whether it exists or works. Advanced semiconductors have no record of their own: Brazil has no domestic function to classify, so the dependence is recorded where it bites, in bra.sov.ceitec (imports of advanced chips) and bra.sov.public-ai-compute (Nvidia and AMD silicon). Open gaps, in order of how much they would change a classification: the software and hardware stack under gov.br and Pix; the current foreign enricher for Angra 2 and Resende's capacity in SWU; who makes the soybean inoculants; owned against chartered FPSOs; the E2's final assembly and Brazilian value share; CEITEC's process node and equipment vendors; MSG GOV's hosting. Update rule: every record is re-checked by 31 October each year or when its status changes; a re-check re-opens every fetched source and moves one that no longer carries its claim to blocked, which turns the stage it held back to unknown.

cases.title: Pix instant payments
cases.function: Settles retail payments between accounts at different institutions in real time, every day of the year, in central bank money, with a directory that resolves Pix keys to accounts.

organizations.name: Banco Central do Brasil
organizations.role: scheme owner, regulator and operator of the SPI settlement system and the DICT key directory

organizations.role: supplier of the platform software and consulting

organizations.role: licensed technology provider connecting institutions to the system

stages.basis: No fetched source settles who controls this stage.
The central bank designed the scheme with participants through consultations and the Fórum Pix; messages follow ISO 20022, an open international standard.

The core runs on Red Hat OpenShift and AMQ Streams under commercial subscription. Both are built on open source (Kubernetes, Apache Kafka), but no source shows the central bank running them without the vendor.
The central bank built the system with Red Hat Consulting, which a central bank official called an active and essential partner.
The central bank launched Pix in November 2020.

The central bank operates the system from two data centres at separate sites, active-active with synchronous replication, a 15 minute recovery time objective and two independent networks from different providers.
Development, maintenance and operation are paid from the central bank's own budget; Red Hat provides technical account management and training.
The scheme rests on Lei 12.865/2013 and central bank resolutions, and the central bank writes its rules.

cases.constraints: The design and the operation sit in the central bank by construction; the software platform under them is a US vendor's commercial distribution of open-source projects. Hardware origin is not on any fetched source.

counterevidence.claim: In July 2025 criminals used compromised credentials at a licensed technology provider, C&M Software, to move funds from banks' reserve accounts through Pix; the central bank let the provider resume under controlled production.
The United States opened a Section 301 investigation in 2025 that cites Pix being both operated and regulated by the central bank.

cases.uncertainty: Research is unknown: no source covers the work before design. Whether any Pix workload sits in Serpro's government cloud is unknown; the TCU cites a Serpro contract with the central bank but no link to Pix. The Red Hat source is vendor marketing.

Every platform is a foreign vendor's product: AWS Outposts, Google Distributed Cloud Hosted, Huawei Cloud Stack and Oracle Dedicated Region Cloud@Customer.
The equipment in the state companies' data centres belongs to the vendors.
The platforms are built and supplied by the vendors and installed in the state companies' facilities.
Installed in Serpro and Dataprev data centres in Brazil, but most vendors sit at one site each: AWS, Huawei and Google only in Brasília at Serpro, Huawei and AWS only in São Paulo at Dataprev.
The state companies custody and manage the equipment, but the TCU found AWS Outposts and Google Distributed Cloud depend on continuous connectivity and send metadata to public regions.
The state companies call on the vendors for technical support and component updates.

Portaria SGD/MGI 5.950/2023 requires storage in Brazil and keeps classified data off public cloud, but the AWS contracts' confidentiality exceptions admit disclosure under foreign orders such as the US CLOUD Act, and the TCU ordered them amended.
